qt: to the Commission Jutta Paulus (Verts/ALE), Manuela Ripa (Verts/ALE), Malte Gallée (Verts/ALE), Anna DeparnayGrunenberg (Verts/ALE), Bas Eickhout (Verts/ALE), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Maria Arena (S&D), Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Maria Noichl (S&D), Pierre Larrouturou (S&D), Anja Hazekamp (The Left), Róża Thun und Hohenstein (Renew) Subject:

Lead is highly toxic and there is no safe level of exposure for humans, which is why it has been banned from petrol, paint and pipes. However, 44 000 tonnes of lead continue to be dispersed into the EU environment every year through hunting, sport shooting and fishing. Owing to the identified uncontrolled risk to the environment and human health from these uses of lead, the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) published the Annex XV Restriction Report in 2021, which proposed a restriction on the use and sale of both lead ammunition and fishing weights in the EU. ECHA’s expert committees then thoroughly reviewed the Annex XV Restriction Report and produced their opinions in December 2022, which supported ECHA’s recommendations. The Commission, led by its Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs, is now expected to publish a draft amendment to Annex XVII of the Regulation on the registration, evaluation, authorisation and restriction of chemicals (REACH) based on the evidence and recommendations provided by ECHA. However, this proposal has been repeatedly delayed, continuing to put the health of European citizens and wildlife at risk. Will the Commission urgently release its proposal on the restriction of lead in outdoor shooting and fishing?
at: (English version) to the Commission Jutta Paulus (Verts/ALE), Manuela Ripa (Verts/ALE), Malte Gallée (Verts/ALE), Anna Deparnay-Grunenberg (Verts/ALE), Bas Eickhout (Verts/ALE), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Maria Arena (S&D), Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Maria Noichl (S&D), Pierre Larrouturou (S&D), Anja Hazekamp (The Left), Róża Thun und Hohenstein (Renew) (19 February 2024) Subject: REACH restriction on lead in outdoor shooting and fishing Lead is highly toxic and there is no safe level of exposure for humans, which is why it has been banned from petrol, paint and pipes. However, 44 000 tonnes of lead continue to be dispersed into the EU environment every year through hunting, sport shooting and fishing. (11 April 2024) The Commission has been assessing the recommendations of the European Chemicals Agency and its scientific committees for a restriction of lead ammunition and fishing tackle and is still discussing the most appropriate measures to be included in a legal proposal. The Commission is committed to carefully listening to the European Parliament and Member States’ concerns, as well as to other stakeholders’, in order to ensure that any resulting proposal is balanced and considers all the impacts of the proposed measures. The Commission remains committed to reduce the risks from lead to human health and the environment and is doing its outmost to progress rapidly with this restriction.
